p.src: The dice players shouted for aces and sixes, while the coin tossers called out heads and backs; some traded insults amid laughter, while others came to earnest blows. The losers pawned coats and robes, stripped off kerchiefs and even socks, all to win back their losses. They abandoned their livelihoods and forgot food and sleep, yet ended with nothing but loss; The winners strutted triumphantly, swaggering here and there as they sought another drinking companion and another game. Their purses, sashes, and sleeves bulged with silver and cash, but when the stakes were recovered and accounts settled, they had won little: the croupiers and money changers had skimmed off the profit. Leaving the gambling scene aside, village girls and farmwives had abandoned hoeing wheat and watering vegetables. In twos and threes they formed groups, standing blankly with faces black as mud and teeth yellow as gold, waiting for the actress to appear. They wondered: she too was born and raised by parents like us, so how could she be so beautiful that so many people came to see her? That day not only people from the nearby villages but townsfolk too came rushing out to watch, trampling bare more than ten mu of green wheat.

p.src: But enough of these details. Wang Qing idly watched for a while until his fingers began to itch. Inside the stage enclosure, amid the crowd, he saw a burly man sitting on a stool with both hands braced upon a table. The fellow had round eyes, a broad face, wide shoulders, and a narrow waist. On the table lay five strings of cash, a dice bowl, and six dice, but nobody was gambling with him. Wang Qing thought, “It has been more than ten months since I got into trouble with the law, and I have not played this game once. I still have the ingot Brother Fan Quan gave me the other day to buy firewood. I will use it for a stake, throw a few rounds with that rogue, and win a few strings to buy fruit.” Wang Qing took out the silver, tossed it onto the table, and said to the man, “Let us have a casual round.” The man shot Wang Qing a glance and said, “If you want to throw, come on.” Before he had finished speaking, another man pushed out from the crowd around a table ahead. He was tall and strongly built and looked rather like the seated fellow. He said to Wang Qing, “Friend, how can he stake against an ingot like that? Give me the silver; I have cash here. If you win, I ask only twenty cash interest on each string.” “Excellent!” said Wang Qing. He exchanged his silver with the man for two strings of cash, though the man had already deducted twenty cash from each string. “So be it,” said Wang Qing. He then agreed with the big fellow to play Vermilion Den. They had thrown only two or three bowls when another man squeezed in, put up a stake, and joined the throwing. Wang Qing was a seasoned gambler from the Eastern Capital. He trusted that the bowl was honest, knew how to dodge and feint, and was sly and deceitful enough to cheat when placing his stake; Amid the commotion the money changer slipped away to another table. The man who had joined them said Wang Qing was throwing too fiercely, withdrew his stake, and merely took a commission for the big fellow. In one run Wang Qing won two strings of cash. His luck was in, and the better he threw, the stronger his cast became: three reds and four-of-a-kind kept tumbling out. The big fellow grew frantic to recover his capital, but every cast brought hopelessly losing little fours that never left his hand. Wang Qing threw nine points, while the fellow perversely answered with an inverted eight. In less than an hour he had lost all five strings of cash. Having won, Wang Qing threaded two strings onto a cord and set them aside, intending to find the fellow who held his ingot and redeem it; then he securely strung the remaining three. Just as he was about to shoulder the money, the defeated fellow shouted, “Where do you think you are taking that cash? Perhaps it has only just come from the furnace and is hot enough to scorch your hands.” Wang Qing said angrily, “You lost it to me, so why are you spouting that damned nonsense?” The fellow bulged his fierce round eyes and cursed, “You dog-begotten whelp! How dare you insult your grandfather!” Wang Qing cursed back, “You country bumpkin! Perhaps I should fear that if you punch me in the belly, you will never pull your fist out? I am taking the money!” The fellow raised both fists and swung straight at Wang Qing’s face. Wang Qing turned sideways and slipped aside, caught the fellow’s arm with the movement, drove his right elbow into the man’s chest, and at the same instant hooked the fellow’s left foot with his own right foot. The fellow possessed only brute strength and knew nothing of such throws. With a thud he toppled backward, face to the sky and back on the ground. The people who had gathered to watch all burst out laughing. The fellow was about to struggle up, but Wang Qing stepped forward, pinned him down, and rained blows upon the tender spots. The man who had changed the money earlier came running over, but instead of making peace or lending help, he snatched up all the cash from the table. Wang Qing flew into a rage, abandoned the man on the ground, and strode after him. Suddenly a woman darted from the crowd and shouted, “You rogue, cease your insolence! I am here!” Wang Qing looked at the woman. What was she like?

p.src: Her great eyes flashed savagely; her thick, coarse brows bristled with murderous menace. Her waist was thick and clumsy, utterly devoid of graceful charm; Her facial skin was coarse and thick, concealed only beneath a layer of powder and rouge. Strange hairpins and rings filled her hair, while fashionable tame bracelets showed upon both arms. She often shifted stone mortars, laughing at how quickly others lost their breath; She regularly lifted well curbs and boasted that her own strength made light of it. She knew not how to ply needle and thread; kicking legs and swinging fists were her special skills.

p.src: The woman was about twenty-four or twenty-five years old. She stripped off her outer jacket, rolled it into a bundle, and tossed it onto a table. Underneath she wore close-fitting narrow sleeves like arrow shafts and a short parrot-green jacket, with broad-crotched, lined purple silk trousers below. She strode forward, raised her fists, and attacked Wang Qing. Wang Qing saw that she was a woman and that her very first punch left an opening. Meaning to toy with her, he deliberately refrained from using a swift throw. Instead he raised both fists, assumed a guard, displayed his techniques, and grappled with her. And so it appeared:

p.src: They spread into the Great Four-Level stance and kicked with paired flying feet. The Immortal Points the Way; Laozi Rides the Crane. The Twisted Phoenix Elbow struck close at the heart; the Head-on Cannon drove toward the brow. A raised heel brought forth the Ground-Quenching Dragon; a twisted wrist upheld the Heaven-Bearing Bellows. On this side the woman performed Scattered Blossoms Covering the Crown; over here the man played Coiling the Rope Around the Waist. The pair resembled fans pressed flat by the wind; before long, they were like blossoms falling beneath a driving rain.

p.src: By then the songstress had gone onto the stage to perform a comic farce. When the crowd saw a man and woman wrestling over here, they all came running and formed a ring around the pair to watch. The woman saw that Wang Qing could do no more than ward and parry, and lacked the skill to break through her guard. Watching for an opening, she launched the move called “Black Tiger Steals the Heart,” driving a fist straight at Wang Qing’s chest. Wang Qing twisted aside. The woman struck empty air and could not draw back her fist in time. Seizing the moment, Wang Qing caught and twisted her fast, then brought her crashing down with a single throw; just as she touched the ground, he smoothly scooped her up again. This move is called “The Tiger Clasps Its Head.” “Best not soil your clothes,” said Wang Qing. “Do not blame me for handling you roughly—you were the one who came looking for me.” The woman showed not the least trace of shame or anger. Instead, she praised Wang Qing: “Well, well! What splendid fighting skill! “You truly have strength in every sinew and joint!” The two men—the one who had lost his money and been beaten, and the one who had opened the purse and snatched the silver—pushed through the crowd together and strode forward, shouting, “You bastard spawn of donkeys and cattle! How dare you! “How dare you throw our sister to the ground?” Wang Qing shouted back, “You filthy village cuckolds! You lost, robbed me of my money, and now you spew abuse besides!” He rushed forward, drew back his fist, and struck. Suddenly a man burst from the crowd and thrust himself crosswise between the three and their six fists, crying at the top of his voice, “Elder Brother Li, you must not behave so rudely! “Second Brother Duan, Fifth Brother Duan, do not raise your hands either! “You are all men of the same soil. Whatever the matter is, talk it over calmly!” When Wang Qing looked, he saw it was Fan Quan. The three men duly stayed their hands. Fan Quan hastily saluted the woman. “My respects, Third Sister.” The woman returned his greeting and asked, “Is Elder Brother Li a kinsman of yours, Master Fan?” “He is my younger cousin,” Fan Quan replied. “What exceptional fighting skill!” said the woman. Wang Qing said to Fan Quan, “That scoundrel lost his money himself, yet had his accomplice snatch it back.” Fan Quan laughed. “That is how Second Brother and Fifth Brother make their living. Why did you interfere with them?” Over to one side, Duan the Second and Duan the Fifth stared at their sister with all four eyes. The woman said, “Out of respect for Master Fan, there is no need to quarrel with him any further. “Bring me that ingot of silver!” Seeing his sister urge him to yield, and seeing how formidable she was, Duan the Fifth thought, “I lost it fairly, after all.” He had no choice but to take out the original ingot and hand it to his sister, Third Sister Duan. Third Sister Duan gave it to Fan Quan and said, “Here is the original silver. Take it away!” With that, she took Duan the Second and Duan the Fifth by the arms, parted the crowd, and left. Fan Quan likewise took Wang Qing by the arm and went straight back to the country manor.

p.src: Fan Quan reproached Wang Qing: “For my mother’s sake, I have taken a risk as vast as a sea of blood by keeping you here, brother; “if an amnesty should be granted, I mean to make arrangements for you again. “Yet how can you be so utterly unable to sit still? “Duan the Second and Duan the Fifth are the most crafty and vicious of men; “and their sister, Third Sister Duan, is more ruthless still. People have given her the nickname ‘Tiger’s Lair.’ “Heaven knows how many sons of decent families she has lured into her snares. “When she was fifteen, she married a husband; “the man proved a thorough fool, and before a year had passed, she had tormented him to death. “Relying on her great strength, she and Duan the Second and Duan the Fifth make a business of prowling about, stirring up fights, and earning dirty money. “What village anywhere nearby does not fear them? “They hired that songstress solely to lure people into gambling. “Every gaming table there is part of their trap. “And yet you went there, brother, and invited trouble! “If by any chance you betray yourself, the calamity that will befall you and me will be no small matter.” Wang Qing was left speechless by Fan Quan’s rebuke. Fan Quan rose and said to Wang Qing, “I must go into the prefectural city to report for duty. I shall come and see you again tomorrow.”

p.src: Leaving aside Fan Quan’s entry into Fangzhou, let us speak of Wang Qing, who rested when night fell that day and passed an uneventful night. The next day, just as he finished washing and combing his hair, a servant reported, “Old Master Duan has come to see the young master.” Wang Qing had no choice but to go out and receive him; he proved to be an old man with a wrinkled face and silvery beard. After exchanging courtesies, host and guest took their appointed seats. Old Master Duan looked Wang Qing over from head to foot and exclaimed, “A truly imposing fellow!” He then asked where Wang Qing came from, why he had come there, how Steward Fan was related to him, and whether he had ever taken a wife. Finding these questions suspicious, Wang Qing concocted a whole string of lies and answered evasively, “I am a native of the Western Capital. Both my parents are dead, and my wife has also passed away. Constable Fan and I are cousins through our mothers. Last year, when Constable Fan went to the Western Capital on official business, he saw that I was all alone with no one to care for me, and specially brought me here. I have some skill with fists and staves, and when a suitable opportunity arises, I mean to seek a position in this prefecture.” Old Master Duan was delighted by what he heard. After asking Wang Qing’s age and birth horoscope, he took his leave. Some time later, while Wang Qing was still puzzling over the visit, another man pushed open the door and entered, asking, “Is Steward Fan here? And is this the young master Li?” The two stared at each other in astonishment, each thinking, “I have met him before.” They had only just exchanged courtesies and were about to question each other when Fan Quan happened to arrive. When all three were seated, Fan Quan asked, “Master Li, what brings you here?” At these words, Wang Qing suddenly remembered: “He is Li Zhu, the fortune-teller.” Li Zhu also recalled, “He is a man from the Eastern Capital, surnamed Wang, who once consulted me about his fortune.” Li Zhu said to Fan Quan, “Steward, I have not had the chance to visit you for quite some time. May I ask whether you have a young relative named Li?” Pointing at Wang Qing, Fan Quan replied, “This is my kinsman, young Master Li.” Wang Qing promptly added, “My true surname is Li. Wang was my maternal grandfather’s surname.” Li Zhu clapped his hands and laughed. “What a poor memory I have! I thought your surname was Wang and that we had once met before Kaifeng Prefecture in the Eastern Capital.” Seeing that he had recounted the details, Wang Qing lowered his head and said nothing. Li Zhu said to Wang Qing, “After we parted, I returned to Jingnan, where I met an extraordinary master who taught me swordsmanship and the subtle art of reading destinies by the Ziping method. That is why people now call me ‘Master Golden Sword.’ Lately I have been in Fangzhou. Hearing how lively things were here, I came especially to ply my trade during the festival. The Duan brothers learned that I knew swordsmanship and wanted me to teach them fencing, so they kept me at their home. Just now Old Master Duan returned and asked me to calculate your horoscope. Where could one find another birth chart so auspicious? In time, your rank and honor will be beyond words. At present the Red Phoenix star shines upon you, so a joyful occasion must be at hand. Third Mistress Duan and Old Master Duan were overjoyed and wish to take you into their family as a son-in-law. Taking advantage of this auspicious day, I have come expressly to act as matchmaker. Third Mistress’s horoscope will bring exceptional prosperity to her husband. I compared the two just now: a copper basin and an iron broom—truly a perfectly matched pair. Do let me bring the match about, so that I may drink a cup of wedding wine!” After hearing this speech, Fan Quan pondered for a while and thought, “The Duan family are fierce and unruly. If I refuse this marriage and some flaw in our story is exposed, the harm will be considerable. I can only turn circumstances to our advantage!” He therefore said to Li Zhu, “So that is how matters stand! We are deeply obliged to Old Master Duan and Third Mistress for their kind intentions. But this kinsman of mine is rough and foolish. How could he be fit to become their honored son-in-law?” Li Zhu said, “Oh, come now! Steward, you need not be so modest. Over there, Third Mistress has been praising the young master without cease!”

I compared the two just now: a copper basin and an iron broom—truly a perfectly matched pair.
Do let me bring the match about, so that I may drink a cup of wedding wine!”

After hearing this speech, Fan Quan pondered for a while and thought, “The Duan family are fierce and unruly. If I refuse this marriage and some flaw in our story is exposed, the harm will be considerable.
I can only turn circumstances to our advantage!”
He therefore said to Li Zhu, “So that is how matters stand!
We are deeply obliged to Old Master Duan and Third Mistress for their kind intentions.
But this kinsman of mine is rough and foolish. How could he be fit to become their honored son-in-law?”
Li Zhu said, “Oh, come now!
Steward, you need not be so modest.
Over there, Third Mistress has been praising the young master without cease!”

p.src: Fan Quan said, “Then this is excellent! I can act as his guardian and arrange the marriage.” He took a five-tael ingot of silver from his person and offered it to Li Zhu, saying, “There is little in this village with which to entertain you. Please accept this trifling token for tea and refreshments; when the affair succeeds, I shall reward you handsomely.” Li Zhu protested, “How could I possibly accept this?” Fan Quan replied, “Forgive the inadequacy of my offering! I ask only one thing: do not tell them that he has used two surnames, and kindly see that everything is handled smoothly.” Li Zhu was an astrologer and fortune-teller. Once he had the silver, he thanked Fan Quan and Wang Qing profusely, took his leave, and returned to the Duan family estate to report. He cared nothing about one surname or two, or whether a man was good or bad; his sole concern was to broker matches, cadge food and wine, and earn copper cash. Moreover, Third Mistress Duan herself had taken a fancy to her match, and everyone in the household had always feared her. Even Old Master Duan dared not oppose her, so the matter was settled as soon as it was proposed.

p.src: Li Zhu went back and forth between the two households to negotiate the match, hoping to talk up the betrothal gifts, for only then would the matchmaker prosper. Fan Quan feared that sending betrothal gifts would draw attention and cause trouble, so he arranged for both families to dispense with them altogether. Old Master Duan was a thrifty householder and all the more delighted; he proceeded directly to choose a wedding day. They chose the twenty-second of that month. Sheep and pigs were slaughtered, fish netted and frogs caught; they prepared only great bowls of wine and heaping platters of meat and invited male and female relatives to the wedding feast. Pipes, flutes, drums, bands, bridal chamber, and flower candles were all dispensed with. Fan Quan had a new suit of clothes made for Wang Qing and escorted him to the Duan family estate. As official business demanded his attention, Fan Quan took his leave and departed first. Wang Qing and Third Mistress Duan performed the mutual bows, shared the nuptial cup, and completed the other rites, all in a perfunctory fashion. Old Master Duan laid out a feast in the thatched hall. With more than twenty relatives, his own sons, his new son-in-law, and the matchmaker Li Zhu, he drank there all day, and the company dispersed only at dusk. Those relatives who lived nearby all said their farewells and left; those who lived too far away to make the journey home were the husband and wife Fang Han, the bride’s aunt and uncle; her cousin Qiu Xiang and his wife; and Shi Jun, the brother-in-law of Second Duan, with his wife. The three men lodged in the eastern wing outside; The three women, none of them particularly sedate, carried wine and food to Wang Qing and Third Mistress Duan to warm the bridal chamber. Laughing and joking, they drank for another while before finally clearing up and retiring. Maidservants and old serving women entered the bridal chamber to make the bed and fold the quilts, then invited the bridegroom and bride to retire. A maid pulled the door shut from outside, and they all discreetly withdrew.

p.src: Third Mistress Duan had mixed freely with people from childhood and, moreover, was an experienced woman. Accustomed to such matters, she felt no particular shame and promptly removed her hairpins and bracelets and took off her jacket. Wang Qing was a dissolute young rake, and since falling foul of the law he had gone without a woman for more than ten months. Though Third Mistress Duan, with her thick brows and large eyes, could not compare in seductive grace and slender beauty with the lovely Lady Niu, when Wang Qing saw her before the lamp bare her chest, untie her red bodice, and expose her smooth white breasts, lust surged within him, and he reached out to embrace her. Third Mistress Duan slapped Wang Qing across the face and said, “Stop pawing at me! What is your hurry?” The two embraced, climbed onto the bed, slipped beneath the covers, and shared the pleasures of the pillow. Just as the verse says:

p.src: One was a village woman who had lost her chastity, the other a convicted soldier guilty of violence. Both had faces three feet thick and feet alike ten inches long. This one truly panted and cried herself hoarse, sounding like an ox snorting beneath a willow; that one feigned coy and faltering words, just like an oriole warbling among the flowers. With no silken stockings on, she bared a pair of bare feet upon his shoulders; her golden hairpin slipped backward, and beside the pillow lay piled a cloud of raven hair. Though they knew nothing of vows sworn by sea and mountain, they still contrived a thousand amorous charms; with no coy shame before cloud and rain, they performed ten thousand forms of dalliance.

p.src: That night, outside the bridal chamber, another laughably absurd incident occurred. The wives of Fang Han, Qiu Xiang, and Shi Jun were all young. Their faces flushed from drinking, and instead of going to bed, they pulled along the wives of Duan Er and Duan Wu, crept quietly outside the bridal chamber, and pressed their ears to the partition to listen; every sound within the room was heard by them in the clearest detail. Wang Qing was a dissolute fellow well versed in the arts of the bedchamber; when he saw his wife yield to him, he exerted himself to please her. The women outside listened until matters reached their deepest intensity, and before they knew it even their silken drawers were soaked through.

p.src: The women were still joking and teasing, pinching and pawing at one another, when Duan Er suddenly rushed in and shouted, “What are we to do! What are we to do! You women have no idea how grave this is, yet you are still laughing and fooling around here!” The women all broke into a cold sweat, unable to understand what was happening. Duan Er shouted again, “Sister! Third Sister! Get up at once! You have brought a seed of disaster into your bed!” Duan Sanniang was just at the height of her pleasure and instead reproached Duan Er, answering from the bed, “What can have happened at this hour that makes you raise such a commotion?” Duan Er shouted once more, “The fire is singeing the bird’s feathers! Yet you still do not know whether you are dead or alive!” Wang Qing already had a guilty conscience. He told his wife to dress, and they came out together to ask what was wrong; all the women scattered and fled. The moment Wang Qing stepped through the door, Duan Er seized him by one hand and dragged him to the thatched hall in front. There Fan Quan was lamenting and protesting, frantic as an ant on a hot pan, with nowhere to turn. Old Master Duan, Duan Wu, and Duan Sanniang arrived close behind. It turned out that Huang Da, from east of Gongjia Village in Xin’an County, had recovered from the wounds inflicted upon him. After discovering Wang Qing’s exact whereabouts, he had gone to Fangzhou the previous night and informed the prefect. The prefect, Zhang Guxing, endorsed an official warrant and immediately dispatched the chief constable with local troops to arrest the murderer Wang Qing, as well as Fan Quan and the Duan household for harboring a criminal. Because Fan Quan was on good terms with Clerk Xue, who handled cases in that prefecture, the clerk had secretly leaked the news to him beforehand. Fan Quan abandoned his wife and children and fled here like a puff of smoke. The government troops would arrive at any moment! Every one of them would be dragged into a criminal case! They stamped their feet and beat their chests. It was as if a brooding hen’s nest had been overturned, throwing them all into wild confusion. They cursed Wang Qing and heaped shame upon Sanniang. Amid the uproar, the fortune-teller Li Zhu, known as “Master Golden Sword,” emerged from the eastern wing outside the thatched hall. Stepping forward, he said, “If you gentlemen wish to escape disaster, you must heed a word from me!” They all crowded around him at once and asked what he meant. Li Zhu said, “Since matters have come to this, of all the thirty-six stratagems, flight is best!” They asked, “Where can we flee?” Li Zhu replied, “Twenty li west of here stands Mount Fang.” They said, “That is a haunt of outlaws.” Li Zhu laughed. “How foolish you all are! Do you still expect to remain respectable folk now?” They asked, “Then what do you propose?” Li Zhu said, “Liao Li, the chief of the Mount Fang stronghold, is fairly well acquainted with me. He commands five or six hundred followers, whom the government troops have been unable to suppress. There is no time to lose. Quickly gather your valuables and other belongings, and let us all go there and join his band. Only then can we escape this great calamity.” Fang Han and the other six men and women feared that their relatives might later be arrested and implicated. Wang Qing and Duan Sanniang also urged them most vehemently. With no other course open, they all had to take this road. They immediately gathered every valuable and portable possession in the manor, whether of worth or not, and had it all packed up; at the same time, they lit thirty or forty torches. The nine—Wang Qing, Duan Sanniang, Duan Er, Duan Wu, Fang Han, Qiu Xiang, Shi Jun, Li Zhu, and Fan Quan—made themselves ready. Each strapped a saber to the waist and took a broad-bladed polearm from the rack. They summoned the manor servants, of whom more than forty were willing to go, and all bound up their clothes and leggings for travel. Wang Qing, Li Zhu, and Fan Quan led the way, while Fang Han, Qiu Xiang, and Shi Jun guarded the women in the middle. Fortunately, the five women all had feet as broad as hoes and could walk every bit as well as the men. Duan Sanniang, Duan Er, and Duan Wu brought up the rear. They set fire to both the front and back of the manor and raised a great shout; then the whole company, weapons in hand, surged westward.

p.src: Wang Qing and his company had gone only four or five li when they encountered the chief constable and his local troops, with Huang Da accompanying them to make the arrests. The chief constable stepped forward, but Wang Qing’s blade rose and fell, cleaving him into two pieces. Li Zhu, Duan Sanniang, and the others rushed forward together and scattered the local troops. p.src: By the time Wang Qing and his company reached the foot of the Mount Fang stronghold, it was already the fifth watch. Li Zhu proposed that he first go up the mountain alone and appeal to Liao Li; only then would it be safe to lead the rest up to join the band. The young bandits patrolling inside the stronghold saw a confusion of torchlight below the mountain and hurried to inform their chief. Liao Li suspected they were government troops. Accustomed as he was to despising them as useless, he hurriedly rose, donned his armor, seized his spear, opened the stockade gate, mustered his followers, and descended the mountain to meet the enemy. Seeing lights flare upon the mountain and many men descending, Wang Qing made ready in advance. Presently Liao Li came straight to the foot of the mountain. Seeing the great number of men and women, he judged that they were not government troops. Leveling his spear, Liao Li shouted, “You wretched pack of men and women! How dare you disturb my stronghold and dig earth upon the Grand Duke’s head?” Li Zhu stepped forward, bowed, and said, “Great King, it is your unworthy younger brother, Li Zhu.” He then briefly related how Wang Qing had committed his crime and killed the prison commandant and the government troops. When Liao Li heard from Li Zhu how formidable Wang Qing was, and that he also had the Duan brothers assisting him, he thought, “I stand alone. I fear that in days to come I shall be bullied by them.” His face darkened, and he said to Li Zhu, “This humble place of mine has no room for you people.” Hearing this, Wang Qing thought to himself, “There is only this one master in the stronghold. If I first dispose of him, why should I worry about the underlings?” He leveled his broad-bladed polearm and charged straight at Liao Li. Liao Li flew into a rage and twirled his spear to meet him. Fearing that Wang Qing might come to harm, Duan Sanniang rushed in with her broad-bladed polearm to help him. The three fought for more than ten bouts, and of the three, one fell. Indeed, the earthen jar forever visiting the well must break there, and the outlaw is bound to perish before the arrowhead. But which one of the three fell? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
